did: I built the zoom half of RR31. When the Rust essay restates a ticket, the picture can now be the phone's own Rust Rounds card, photographed by W1's capture, with HyperFrames easing in to the question, each point, the code and the compiler's error, then back out. It renders the same bytes every time, keeps clear of the captions, and any video's cut list can place it. A mock-card sample is proven in CI. Without the week's photographs the essay renders exactly as before.

calls.title: How fast the zoom moves and how long it rests
options: The whole card for a beat, 1.2 s moves, even holds, slowing at most to 0.6 pace and dropping the last stops
Holds timed to the narration's words
calls.why: Timing to the words needs cues the weekly routine doesn't write yet, and one region per scene would change the essay's timing.
calls.undo: Change the numbers in the screen-zoom composition (C795).

calls.title: How close the zoom comes
options: A 24 px margin all round, at most 1.25 screen pixels to a card pixel, clipped above the captions
Fill the frame and let captions draw over the card
calls.why: The margin keeps a point's list number in view, the cap keeps code sharp, and captions stay readable.
calls.undo: Change the margin and cap in the screen-zoom composition (C796).

calls.title: Which essay scenes show the phone's card
options: Question scenes only: question, points, code, then rustc's errors
Also send deep dives to the compiler errors
calls.why: Nothing in a dive says it is about a compile error, and a dive's own code is never on the phone, so pointing a dive at the card would be a guess.

left: Deep dives keep their usual picture: a dive has no field linking it to a compiler error, and its own code is never on the phone (#3288's gap).
Cards essays can't place the zoom yet: home keeps no screenshots for one. W6 builds that next.
The zoom shows on home only once its render pin moves to the image this publishes, the same move server#1049 waits on.
